result_expr: C(phi(x, y, z, t), T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(T(x, y, z, t), t) - Derivative(k(phi(x, y, z, t), T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(T(x, y, z, t), x), x) - Derivative(k(phi(x, y, z, t), T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(T(x, y, z, t), y), y) - Derivative(k(phi(x, y, z, t), T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(T(x, y, z, t), z), z) - rho_i*L(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), t)

symbols.name: C(phi, T)
symbols.meaning: effective volumetric heat capacity, phi*rho_i*c_i + (1-phi)*(rho_v*c_v + rho_a*c_a)

symbols.name: k(phi, T)
symbols.meaning: effective thermal conductivity of the ice/gas mixture

symbols.name: L(T)
symbols.meaning: latent heat of sublimation per unit mass, h_v(T) - h_i(T)

steps.operation: definition of the enthalpy density of the mixture

steps.statement: q = -k(phi,T)*grad T + h_v(T)*j  [W m^-2], where j is the diffusive vapor mass flux
steps.operation: constitutive flux: Fourier conduction plus enthalpy carried by vapor
energy conservation over a fixed control volume, then the divergence theorem
air mass conservation with air at rest
subtract h_v times S4 and h_a times S5 (both zero)

steps.statement: C dT/dt - div(k grad T) - rho_i*L dphi/dt + c_v j.grad T = 0, with C = phi rho_i c_i + (1-phi)(rho_v c_v + rho_a c_a) and L = h_v - h_i
steps.operation: product and chain rule with c_k = dh_k/dT and rho_i constant; SymPy residual 0 (scratch/check.py)

steps.statement: C(phi,T) dT/dt - div(k(phi,T) grad T) - rho_i L(T) dphi/dt = 0
steps.operation: drop vapor enthalpy transport (relative size about 2e-6)

steps.statement: R = C T_t - (k T_x)_x - (k T_y)_y - (k T_z)_z - rho_i L phi_t; every term is in W m^-3 (pint)
steps.operation: expand the divergence in 3D Cartesian coordinates

assumptions_used: Ice is rigid, at rest, and has constant density rho_i (needed in S7)
Gas is at rest on average: vapor moves only by a diffusive flux j, and air has no net flux
Local thermal equilibrium: one temperature T for ice and gas
Low pressure: enthalpy is used in place of internal energy, and pressure work is neglected
Fourier conduction with an effective conductivity k(phi, T)

neglected.effect: Enthalpy transport by vapor diffusion, c_v j . grad T
neglected.why: Ratio to conduction is about c_v*D*rho_v/k ~ 1850*1e-3*1.7e-6/2 ~ 2e-6 near 200 K
The gas is assumed to be at rest. The Peclet number is tiny at near-vacuum pore pressures.
Vapor pressure is about 0.2 Pa near 200 K, so p/rho_v relative to L is about RT/(M L) ~ 0.03 for vapor. Its contribution is further weighted by rho_v/rho_i ~ 1e-9 in the energy content.

neglected.effect: Heat capacity of the gas phase inside C
neglected.why: Kept in C for generality, but rho_v c_v / C is about 1.6e-9
Of order 4*sigma*T^3*d ~ 1e-5 W/m/K for 100 um pores at 200 K, small next to the ice conductivity of about 2 W/m/K

neglected.effect: Interfacial (surface) energy and curvature (Gibbs-Thomson) corrections to L
neglected.why: Of order gamma/(rho_i L r) ~ 0.1/(917*2.8e6*1e-6) ~ 4e-5 relative, for micron-scale curvature
Volumetric expansion coefficient is about 1e-4 per K, which is a small change over the temperature ranges considered
